subject.title: fix(streaming): preserve paragraph separators across block-chunk deliveries [AI-assisted]

question: Should block-streaming preserve paragraph boundaries as in-band text, reserve separator width during splitting, or carry explicit boundary metadata through delivery?
rationale: The bug and affected layer are source-proven, but the near-maxChars case forces a contract choice because naive text-only preservation either exceeds the cap or drops the boundary.

options.title: Choose a complete boundary contract
options.body: Require this PR or a replacement to preserve separators across maxChars boundary cases without exceeding delivery limits, with regression coverage for that exact case.

options.title: Consolidate with the sibling PR
options.body: Compare this branch with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94247 and keep one canonical implementation before merging either candidate.

options.title: Accept a partial repair knowingly
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally land the common-case text-only fix while leaving the maxChars boundary as explicit remaining work on the canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Choose a complete boundary contract
recommendation.body: Require this PR or a replacement to preserve separators across maxChars boundary cases without exceeding delivery limits, with regression coverage for that exact case.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has strong recent history in coalescing and chunking hardening and is the best available routing owner for the streaming contract choice.
